name: ShadowLab
description: One key and one flat ambient, and nothing else. The key sits at azimuth -90 and elevation 34, which puts the sun exactly to the world's -X at a right angle to the lab camera's view axis: every shadow lies to its caster's RIGHT, along +X, with no Z component at all. Two things in the lab depend on that and neither is cosmetic. Yawing the camera right takes a caster off the left edge of frame BEFORE its own shadow, which is the only camera move that separates 'this object stopped casting' from 'this object left the shot'. And a camera-facing quad -- what the LOD ladder draws at rungs 2 and 3 -- is edge-on to a light perpendicular to the camera, which is the angle at which a billboard's shadow is at its smallest. 34 degrees makes the run 1.482 m of shadow per metre of height, so a caster's length on the ground is a number the lab can predict rather than measure. The ambient is 0.16 and grey: enough that a shadowed surface is readable rather than black, low enough that the lit/shadowed ratio is large and a pixel probe does not have to resolve a few counts.
